name: GP Broadway Mill - Green Bay WI

fieldNotes.location: Roster coords (44.49271,-88.034475, ROOFTOP, movedMeters 222) sit within the mill core on a peninsula along the Fox River. Address 1919 S Broadway, Green Bay WI confirmed. Mill core retained at the given coords.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Large urban tissue mill bounded by S Broadway / a rail line (W) and the Fox River (E). Main truck entrance is off S Broadway near an admin/office building at the NW intersection; the property is a controlled industrial campus. Internal roads have Street View coverage but the public-road perimeter entry is gated/checkpointed.
fieldNotes.guardShack: An admin/office building sits at the main Broadway entrance intersection serving as the entry checkpoint; a dedicated guard booth is consistent with a mill of this trucking volume but not separately resolved — flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Very large multi-building campus: pulp/paper machines, multiple converting plants, multiple finished-goods warehouses, water-treatment clarifiers, office buildings.
fieldNotes.railServed: Active rail line runs along the W boundary beside S Broadway with spurs into the property.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Massive trailer operation — multiple drop yards with dozens of rows; 200+ trailers visible across the site.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Multiple warehouse buildings with extensive dock-door banks and trailers backed in on multiple faces; ~70 estimated, 50+ band confident, exact count low confidence.
fieldNotes.scale: Truck scale expected at this trucking volume; not definitively resolved overhead.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Inbound raw material and outbound finished tissue handled from distinct warehouse/dock clusters on different building faces.
fieldNotes.truckGateCount: At least one main Broadway gate; the large campus likely has a second gate (counted 2, flagged uncertain).
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Very wide paved aprons and multi-lane internal roads provide ample room for express/bypass lanes.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Mill is within the dense urban fabric of Green Bay, surrounded by residential neighborhoods and other industry. Urban.
